title: National Gallery of Canada: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works at the National Gallery of Canada, considered through what they enlarge, surround or nearly hide.
introduction:
A striped ship towers above its painters; a pine spreads across bands of water and sky. One is an industrial object altered for war, the other a landscape motif, yet both dominate through a strong structure that smaller details cannot undo. Placing them together offers a different starting point from treating a national collection as one continuous national style.

This selection from the National Gallery of Canada includes Canadian and international work, portraits as well as landscapes, and images that depart from recognisable objects. Its recurring question is one of scale: what is made large, what remains small, and where does the picture ask attention to settle? It is a partial selection, not a summary of the whole collection.
visitNote: This is a focused selection from a much wider collection, not a survey of all Canadian art. Check current object pages for display locations and loans. The dates refer to the objects’ creation; historical events and literary subjects may belong to a different period.

books.title: The Elements of Drawing
books.author: John Ruskin
books.note: Ruskin’s exercises in observing natural forms provide a useful starting point for Thomson, MacDonald and the landscape paintings. Read his judgments critically beside later artists who simplify or rearrange those forms instead of describing them continuously.

works.title: The Jack Pine
works.credit: Tom Thomson. The Jack Pine. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/tom-thomson/the-jack-pine-1917
works.description: The pine's irregular branches cross a background organised in broad horizontal bands. Tree and distance therefore work differently: one interrupts, the other joins. The image's clarity comes from holding those structures together. Rather than losing its particular shape in a general idea of wilderness, this single tree becomes the means of organising an entire landscape.

works.title: The Death of General Wolfe
works.credit: Benjamin West. The Death of General Wolfe. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The surrounding men direct their gestures and attention toward Wolfe's pale body. This arrangement turns a battlefield death into a scene of collective witnessing. The painting was made after the event and constructs its meaning; convincing uniforms and faces do not make it a literal record of the people present at one instant.

works.title: The Tangled Garden
works.credit: J. E. H. MacDonald. The Tangled Garden. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The drooping plants offer no single clear route through the garden. Leaves, flowers and bright patches overlap, requiring smaller acts of separation. MacDonald gives cultivated growth a density that exceeds easy tidiness. The picture rewards distinguishing neighbouring shapes without expecting the whole garden to resolve into a simple pattern.

works.title: Hope I
works.credit: Gustav Klimt. Hope I. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/gustav-klimt/hope-i
works.description: The pregnant figure is distinctly separated from the dark forms behind her. That contrast prevents the surrounding unease from making the body itself vague. The title's hope is consequently qualified by what accompanies it. Pregnancy and unsettling imagery share a field without settling into an uncomplicated celebration or a single fixed prediction.

works.title: Pavane
works.credit: Jean-Paul Riopelle. Pavane. Image: WikiArt. Copyright protected (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: No represented object tells the eye where to stop. Instead, the three sections and changing concentrations of colour provide different scales of organisation. Individual marks remain distinct within the extensive field. Repetition carries attention across the work, while differences in their density keep it from behaving like a uniformly repeated pattern.

works.title: Dazzleships in Dry Dock at Liverpool
works.credit: Edward Wadsworth. Dazzle-ships in Drydock at Liverpool. Image credit: Edward Wadsworth; Source credit: Self-photographed by Mzajac of original painting.. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The striped hull towers over the people completing its paintwork. Dazzle camouflage was designed to confuse estimates of a ship's course, rather than simply make the vessel disappear. Wadsworth turns that deliberate optical disruption into a clearly organised picture, preserving both the geometric pattern and the enormous object to which it has been applied.

works.title: A Canadian Gun-pit
works.credit: Wyndham Lewis. A Canadian Gun-pit. Image credit: Wyndham Lewis; Source credit: https://www.gallery.ca/collection/artwork/a-canadian-gun-pit. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The soldiers' tasks take their positions from the gun and its surrounding supports. Angular forms pass through bodies, equipment and ground, connecting people to the machinery they operate. The scene is still readable as work performed by individuals, but the weapon determines the shared space within which that work can happen.

works.title: Port of Antwerp
works.credit: Georges Braque. Port of Antwerp. WikiArt source label: Public domain US. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/georges-braque/port-of-antwerp-1906
works.description: The curved foreground railing gives the harbour a near boundary, while the boats and distant buildings occupy stronger fields of colour. Those colours do not have to match ordinary daylight to keep the place legible. The view's structure survives through relations between shapes, even as its hues depart from a restrained description of the waterfront.

works.title: North Sea I: Thunderstorm
works.credit: Max Beckmann. North Sea I (Thunderstorm). Image credit: Max Beckmann; Source credit: https://www.sothebys.com/en/auctions/ecatalogue/2010/impressionist-modern-art-evening-sale-n08675/lot.57.html. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The narrow horizon leaves heavy sky pressing against broken water. Yellowish strokes descend through the clouds, introducing a direction that differs from the sea's rolling movement. Beckmann's emphatic divisions keep the storm structured and resistant. The weather does not dissolve the world into a soft, continuous haze.

works.title: Solstice of the Sunflower
works.credit: Paul Nash. Solstice of the Sunflower. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/paul-nash/solstice-of-the-sunflower-1945
works.description: The sunflower's enlarged head and the sun repeat a circular form at different positions in the landscape. Their resemblance organises the picture, but their scales cannot be reconciled as an ordinary view. Nash makes the connection available through painted invention, bringing plant and celestial body into a relationship that botanical accuracy alone would not produce.

works.title: Portrait of a Man with a Felt Hat
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of a Man with a Felt Hat
works.credit: Lorenzo Lotto. Portrait of a Man with a Felt Hat. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/lorenzo-lotto/portrait-of-a-man-with-a-felt-hat-1541
works.description: The held hat gives one hand a task while the direct gaze establishes another kind of contact. Broad dark clothing frames the face without an elaborate setting to explain the sitter's position. The object participates in the pose rather than merely accompanying it: removing it would change how the body presents itself.

works.title: Portrait of a Gentleman
works.credit: Bronzino. Portrait of a gentleman. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/agnolo-bronzino/portrait-of-a-gentleman
works.description: The small sculpture introduces a second kind of figure beside the living sitter. It connects the portrait to possessions and cultivated display, although it cannot by itself tell us everything the man knew or valued. Bronzino uses that juxtaposition to make social presentation part of the likeness rather than leaving the face to carry it alone.

works.title: Anna Ivanovna Tolstaya
works.credit: Élisabeth Vigée Le Brun. Anna Ivanovna Tolstaya. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The resting head and loose drape suggest informality, yet both belong to a carefully arranged pose. Rocks and trees provide an alternative to an official interior without removing the portrait's control of appearance. The apparent ease is something constructed through the relation between dress, gesture and setting, not proof of an unguarded moment.

works.title: Apple Trees in Bloom
works.credit: Alfred Sisley. Apple Trees in Bloom. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The trunks establish repeated positions across the orchard, while blossoms break their outlines into lighter, less settled areas. No single tree needs to dominate. Depth comes from intervals between them and from small differences in colour, allowing the painting to retain a coherent space without a conspicuous central event.

works.title: September Afternoon, Eastern Townships
works.credit: John Arthur Fraser. September Afternoon, Eastern Townships. Image credit: John Arthur Fraser; Source credit: The AMICA Library. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The resting sheep give the near shore an inhabited scale. Beyond them, water and mountains extend through paler distances, so the view can be followed from small rural particulars to a much broader terrain. The flock matters partly because it does not take over: it supplies a measure for space that exceeds it.

works.title: A Shot in the Dawn, Lake Scugog
works.catalogueTitle: A Shot in the Dawn, Lake Scugog
works.credit: John Arthur Fraser. A Shot in the Dawn, Lake Scugog. Image credit: John Arthur Fraser; Source credit: The AMICA Library. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The figure and dog are small beside the water and wide dawn sky. Without the title, their activity might remain secondary to the changes of light. Naming a shot redirects attention toward an event within the landscape, making a useful distinction between what occupies the most painted space and what words identify as the subject.

works.title: At the Rogers Pass
works.catalogueTitle: At the Rogers Pass, Summit of the Selkirk Range, B.C.
works.credit: John Arthur Fraser. At the Rogers Pass, Summit of the Selkirk Range, B.C.. Image credit: John Arthur Fraser; Source credit: 1. The AMICA Library 2. Musée des beaux-arts du Canada, Ottawa. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Dark conifers establish the near valley before the eye reaches exposed, sunlit mountains. The movement between these bands gives scale without a large foreground person. Fraser makes the peaks seem distant through the ground that must be visually crossed to reach them, rather than relying on their outline alone.

works.title: Edmond Dyonnet
works.credit: George Horne Russell. Edmond Dyonnet. Image credit: George Horne Russell; Source credit: Cybermuse des beaux arts du Canada. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The dark clothing and restrained ground leave the face and collar as the chief areas of light. Small tonal changes have to distinguish the features because few objects offer supplementary information about the sitter. This economy differs from Bronzino's portrait with a sculpture: identity is presented here with much less surrounding display.

works.title: The Raven
works.credit: Odilon Redon. The Raven. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/odilon-redon/the-raven-1882
works.description: The dark bird occupies a confined interior near an open window. Its head and beak remain distinct, concentrating attention on a small, watchful presence. The title carries a literary association, but the image does not need to illustrate an entire story. Enclosure and the bird's position supply a more limited, sustained situation.

works.title: Oedipus Taken Down from the Tree
works.catalogueTitle: Oedipus Taken Down from the Tree
works.credit: Jean-François Millet. Oedipus Taken Down from the Tree. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: A small child's exposed body becomes the point around which the figures gather. Dark branches enclose the group while light clarifies the act of handling and supporting that vulnerable weight. Millet makes the ancient subject intelligible through bodily relations before every detail of the Oedipus story has been identified.

closingSections.title: What a small reproduction cannot measure
paragraphs: Compare these works in Artline, but keep their recorded dimensions nearby: a screen can make a small portrait and a large triptych seem equivalent. For an in-person visit, confirm availability with the gallery. Ownership and a catalogue entry do not necessarily mean a work is currently hanging.
